context: Tests whether the agent recognises a mixed-concern diff (new feature, bug fix, and documentation update) and proposes atomic commits rather than bundling everything into one. Also checks that each resulting commit message follows conventional commit format: correct type prefix, imperative-mood subject under 60 characters, no emoji, and no trailing period.

checklist.name: Multiple commits created
checklist.description: The repository has at least 2 new commits on top of the initial skeleton commit (i.e. git log shows 3 or more commits total), reflecting a split of the mixed concerns

checklist.name: Feature in its own commit
checklist.description: src/feature.py is introduced in a separate commit whose type prefix is 'feat'

checklist.name: Bug fix in its own commit
checklist.description: The whitespace-stripping change to src/parser.py is in a separate commit whose type prefix is 'fix'

checklist.name: No emoji in any commit message
checklist.description: None of the new commit messages (subject or body) contain emoji characters

checklist.name: Subject line imperative mood
checklist.description: Every new commit subject begins with an imperative verb (e.g. 'add', 'fix', 'update') rather than a past-tense or noun form

checklist.name: Subject line lower case
checklist.description: Every new commit subject starts with a lower-case letter (after the type prefix and colon)

checklist.name: Subject line under 60 characters
checklist.description: Every new commit subject (the full first line including type prefix) is under 60 characters - 59 or fewer

checklist.name: No trailing period in subject
checklist.description: No new commit subject line ends with a full stop / period character

checklist.name: All pending files committed
checklist.description: Every pending change is committed - the new src/feature.py, the src/parser.py whitespace fix and the docs/README.md update - with no modified or untracked project files left behind apart from the commit-plan.md artifact the task asks for

checklist.name: commit-plan.md present
checklist.description: A file named commit-plan.md exists in the working directory and contains a rationale for how the changes were split across commits
